stats.text: An estimated 19.1% of US adults had an anxiety disorder in the past year. The rate was higher in women (23.4%) than in men (14.3%). These figures come from interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) data

stats.text: About 2.7% of US adults had panic disorder in the past year, with a higher rate in women (3.8%) than in men (1.6%). These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.

stats.text: About 0.9% of US adults had agoraphobia in the past year. This figure comes from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) data

stats.text: About 2.7% of US adults had generalized anxiety disorder in the past year, with a higher rate in women (3.4%) than in men (1.9%). These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.

stats.text: In 2021, about 21.0 million US adults (8.3%) had at least one major depressive episode in the past year, based on NSDUH data summarized by NIMH. The rate was higher in women (10.3%) than in men (6.2%). A newer 2025 estimate is available on a separate card.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) data

stats.text: In 2025, about 7.4% of US adults aged 18 or older (roughly 19.7 million people) had a major depressive episode in the past year, according to the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. This is the newest national figure (data about one year old). Survey methods change over time, so compare years with care.
stats.publisher: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH)

stats.text: More than 1 billion people around the world were living with a mental health condition, the World Health Organization reported in September 2025. Anxiety and depression were the most common. The estimate is based on 2021 data.
stats.publisher: World Health Organization (WHO)

sources.title: Over a billion people living with mental health conditions – services require urgent scale-up (news release)
World mental health today: latest data

stats.text: In 2021, about 359 million people worldwide were living with an anxiety disorder, including about 72 million children and adolescents. WHO describes anxiety disorders as the most common mental disorders in the world (WHO fact sheets, 2025).
stats.publisher: World Health Organization (WHO)

stats.text: WHO estimates that about 332 million people worldwide live with depression, or roughly 5.7% of adults (4.6% of men and 6.9% of women). The estimate is based on 2021 data (WHO fact sheet, 2025).
stats.publisher: World Health Organization (WHO)

stats.text: About 2.8% of US adults had bipolar disorder in the past year, with similar rates in men and women; about 4.4% have it at some point in life. These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) data

stats.text: In 2023, about 6.0% of US adults (roughly 15.5 million people) reported a current ADHD diagnosis, and about half of them were first diagnosed as adults. This figure is based on self-report in a national survey.
stats.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics Rapid Surveys System (MMWR)

stats.text: About 1.4% of US adults had borderline personality disorder in the past year, and about 9.1% had any personality disorder. These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.

stats.text: About 0.6% of US adults have had anorexia nervosa at some point in life, three times more often women (0.9%) than men (0.3%). The survey did not produce a past-year figure. These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) data

stats.text: About 0.3% of US adults had bulimia nervosa in the past year, and about 1.0% have had it at some point in life. These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) data

stats.text: About 1.2% of US adults had binge-eating disorder in the past year, and about 2.8% have had it at some point in life, making it the most common of these eating disorders. These figures come from NCS-R interviews done in 2001–2003, so the data are more than 20 years old.
stats.publisher: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), using National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) data

stats.text: Estimates of how many people in the US have schizophrenia or a related psychotic disorder range from about 0.25% to 0.64%. NIMH summarizes several US studies (interviews, claims data and records) published between 2005 and 2013, so the figure is a range, not one survey result.

stats.text: In a 2004 national telephone survey of US adults, about 2.4% screened positive for body dysmorphic disorder (2.5% of women, 2.2% of men). The interviews were done by trained lay interviewers, so the authors call for confirmation with clinical interviews.
